_doc: The reflect contract, captured from the PYTHON kernel's own replies (src/lib/python, `kernel/_agent.py` `_apply_reflect_flags` / `_roster`) and reproduced by the ts kernel (tests/reflect.test.ts replays every case from `tree` + `bundles`). DISTILLED by default: `tree` is the roster {id, sentence, description?, mode?, children} (gated per node — see the last case), `kernel_verbs` sorted and cut at the first em-dash, and a `more` line; `detail:"full"` gives the wiring tree and every verb doc whole. `tree` is decided by key presence (absent = all, null/none = omitted), `tree:"ids"` and `bundles` page with `limit`/`after` (`next` / `bundles_next`), `readme` is true | "index" | "<key>" (this kernel's doc tree is empty). Differences BY DESIGN, per runtime: the root's `runtime` ("ts") and handler_module; the kernel verbs this kernel answers (no tree CRUD — the `_` line says so); the bundle catalog; python's root also carries its loader's doc frame (`self_extension`, and `readmes`/`docs` under full), which this kernel has no loader to contribute. The browser kernel has no OS env, so env is always "host" and version null.

kernel_verbs.cancel: args: task_id:int|str. Kills that task AND ITS SUBTREE (a name kills the execution it names)
kernel_verbs.kernel_stop: No args. Stops this kernel gracefully
kernel_verbs.ledger: No args. EVERY execution YOU originated and what it became
kernel_verbs.ps: No args. The live kernel-wide TASK TABLE
kernel_verbs.shutdown_agents: No args. Stops the AGENTS, not the kernel: drains (new roots refused), sends `shutdown` to every agent advertising it, waits for in-flight work, cancels the rest. Returns {drained, shut:[ids], cancelled:[ids]}.

expect.sentence: Fantastic kernel. Everything is reachable by sending messages to agents.

kernel_verbs._: Kernel-owned: send to 'kernel'. The id you name is the OPERAND, not the actor. (`verbs` is what this agent itself does.) This kernel answers the verbs below; tree CRUD lives on the HOST root, reached over the bridge.
kernel_verbs.ps: No args. The live kernel-wide TASK TABLE — {tasks:[{id, agent, parent, verb, started_at}]}, one row per in-flight dispatch; an id is the message id of the call that started it, `parent` chains the rows into the send tree. Paged.
kernel_verbs.cancel: args: task_id:int|str. Kills that task AND ITS SUBTREE (a name kills the execution it names) — returns {cancelled, killed:[ids]}; the blocked caller's item settles status:'cancelled'. An unknown or finished id kills nothing and says so.
kernel_verbs.ledger: No args. EVERY execution YOU originated and what it became — {executions:[{id, target, status, attempts, retries, named, name?, outcome?, acked?}]}, paged, read from the kernel's memory store plus what is not yet flushed. `outcome` keeps the RESULT only for a named call; a dead letter keeps its error; anything else is {status, bytes}. Failed/timed_out/cancelled rows are the dead-letter queue (announced by the `on_deadletter` event): inspect, retry with a NEW id if you choose, then `ack_deadletter` it.
kernel_verbs.ack_deadletter: args: id:int|str (req — an execution id, or its name). Acknowledges a DEAD LETTER you originated — recorded in the kernel's store, it may then be pruned. Returns {acked:true, id}.
kernel_verbs.kernel_start: No args. THE START SEQUENCE — the root must name `memory_store_id` (fail loud otherwise): boots the root (it mints the guid), then that store, starts flushing the kernel's execution rows into it, then boots every other agent in registration order. Idempotent. Returns {started, store, booted:[ids]}.
kernel_verbs.shutdown_agents: No args. Stops the AGENTS, not the kernel: drains (new roots refused), sends `shutdown` to every agent advertising it, waits for in-flight work, cancels the rest. Returns {drained, shut:[ids], cancelled:[ids]}.
kernel_verbs.kernel_stop: No args. Stops this kernel gracefully — drain, every call settles (done, or cancelled into the dead letters), the last rows flush, the flusher stops. A browser kernel has no process to exit: it refuses new work until the page reloads.
